newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's sugar imports to stabilise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's sugar imports to stabilise in 1997.

text.p: Morocco, which imports half of its annual sugar needs, expects raw sugar purchases to stabilise around half a million tonnes in 1997, traders said on Tuesday.

"Taking into account the recent market indicators, we expect Morocco's raw sugar imports to stabilise around half a million tonnes from January to December 1997," a Casablanca-based trader told Reuters.
This is due mainly to an expected good sugar harvest and to a liberalisation programme that is expected to affect domestic consumption, the trader said.
Importers forecast sugar consumption to drop slightly as the authorities would reduce the subsidy in the coming months on imported sugar. That stands at 2,000 dirhams ($217.3) per tonne.
According to the Office des Changes exchange bureau, Morocco imported 512,613 tonnes of raw sugar at a cost of 1.34 billion dirhams from January to December 1996.
"Raw sugar imports rose 7.3 percent in 1996, from 477,700 tonnes in 1995," an official at the bureau said.
